newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin gives Moscow opt-out on housing reform.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin gives Moscow opt-out on housing reform.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has approved Moscow's plans to opt out of the government's controversial housing reform plans, Interfax news agency quoted Mayor Yuri Luzhkov as saying.

"Yeltsin has fully confirmed Moscow's right to carry out housing reform as considered necessary by the city government and the city parliament," Interfax news agency quoted Luzhkov as saying after a meeting with Yeltsin in Kremlin on Tuesday.

Any opt-out is bound to dilute the impact of the planned nationwide housing reforms, which aim to wean local authorities off massive housing subsidies. Rents are to be raised sharply, but targeted subsidies are to be given to the poor.
Russia's new reformist government views the changes as a key part of its reform policy and the plan is being masterminded by young First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov.
But Luzhkov said most people would not be able to afford higher rent, and he pledged to protect the Muscovites at least.
"We are not at odds with the Russian government, we simply have different points of view on the housing reform, and they are not bound to change. We live in a democratic society," he said.

The popular Luzhkov, considered as a likely contender for the presidency in 2000, also won an opt-out for Moscow in Russia's privatisation campaign, when he accused then privatisation boss Anatoly Chubais of selling off Russia's riches for nothing.
